metadata.title: Why Claude's Click Lands in the Wrong Spot — and the One Ratio That Fixes It
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why does Claude's computer-use click land in the wrong spot? Lands the carry-out that the fix is one ratio — original-over-sent, per axis — applied to the model's coordinates before the OS input driver ever sees them.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B04 (the (700,410) sent-raw miss, paid off scaled to (960,540) dead center)

beats.narration_text: People assume Claude's click is just random guessing. It isn't. It's scaling — Claude sees a smaller image than your screen. So why does Claude's click land in the wrong spot?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude's click is just random guessing.', hesitates on 'guessing', corrects to 'scaling', lands the real question

props.text:

just random guessing.

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('guessing' -> 'scaling') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: If Claude returns coordinates for a 1456 by 819 image, how do you translate them onto a 1920 by 1080 screen without the click landing wrong?

shot.new_visual_element: Two labeled rectangles (SENT 1456x819 / SCREEN 1920x1080) with a question mark bridging them

production_viz.label: Two sizes, one question
production_viz.mechanic: Small rectangle labeled 'SENT — 1456 × 819' on the left, large rectangle labeled 'SCREEN — 1920 × 1080' on the right. A crimson question mark sits between them, on a dashed connecting line.

beats.narration_text: Say your screen is 1920 by 1080, but the API only sends Claude a 1456 by 819 view. Claude says click 700, 410. Sent raw, that misses — the coordinates belong to the smaller image, not your screen.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — small SENT rectangle with a dot at (700,410); the raw dot replotted at the same pixel position inside the larger SCREEN rectangle, missing the button

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — sent raw, it misses
production_viz.mechanic: Left: small rectangle 'SENT 1456×819' with a teal dot at (700,410) and a button outline nearby. Right: large rectangle 'SCREEN 1920×1080' with the real button outline; the same raw (700,410) dot, now crimson, plots well off the button. THIS EXACT TWO-RECTANGLE COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: Multiply Claude's coordinates by the ratio original over sent, per axis. That's the inverse of the resize — it maps the smaller image's pixels back onto your real screen.

shot.new_visual_element: Formula card: x' = x · (screen_w / sent_w), y' = y · (screen_h / sent_h)

production_viz.label: The formula
production_viz.mechanic: Centered serif formula card in INK: x′ = x · (screen_w ÷ sent_w) on one line, y′ = y · (screen_h ÷ sent_h) below it. A teal bracket labeled 'INVERSE OF THE RESIZE' spans both lines.

beats.narration_text: Back to 700, 410: scale by 1920 over 1456 and 1080 over 819, and you get 960, 540 — dead center on the button. The same math holds at any resolution: sent at 1456 by 819, a 2560 by 1440 screen still gets a perfect hit.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same SENT/SCREEN composition as B02, the scaled dot now landing on the button; a second, smaller resolution pair confirming the ratio generalizes

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — scaled, it lands
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical — SENT 1456×819 rectangle, SCREEN 1920×1080 rectangle. This time the dot travels from (700,410) through the formula to (960,540), landing teal and dead-center on the button. Beneath it, a smaller confirming pair: '1456×819 → 2560×1440' with its own dot landing on-target.

beats.narration_text: Multiply Claude's coordinates by original over sent, per axis — that inverse ratio is what turns a smaller image's pixels back into your real screen's pixels.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. My computer-use app sends Claude a 1456 by 819 view of a 1920 by 1080 screen. Claude returns click coordinates in the view's coordinate space. Show me the two-line scaling formula I need before passing those coordinates to the OS input driver, and explain what happens if I skip it on a Retina display with a device pixel ratio of two. Liam, in for Bear.
